detection_signals.note: test-automation stacks, not testing in general: a bare tests/ directory, a conftest.py or a pytest.ini would match nearly every repository and make this lens win everywhere, so none of them is a signal here. Every signal names a browser, contract or mutation automation stack that a repository only carries deliberately. Matched by door._path_matches_signal (a signal ending in '/' matches a directory name at any depth, anything else is fnmatch against the basename) and door._manifest_string_hit (substring of a file on door.MANIFEST_FILENAMES). Sorted lens order puts data-science ahead of qa-engineer, and none of these signals overlaps its four, so the data-science fixture is not stolen.

challenge_question: Which failure would be expensive enough that we need an independent oracle rather than implementation-derived expected values?

question_budget.work_shape: QA campaign, regression or exploratory testing (persona doc 3.1 class 12). 4.2 carries no automation row, so the two nearest rows set the budget: 'Manual QA campaign' 1-4 and 'Brownfield feature' 1-4. A high-risk irreversible, security or payment change has no fixed cap under 4.2 and the risk_classes below raise it.

forcing_classes.label: Flaky test waived
forcing_classes.why: the diff adds or widens a skip, an expected failure or a retry on an existing test: @pytest.mark.skip, @pytest.mark.xfail, @pytest.mark.flaky, unittest.skip, test.skip(, it.skip(, xit(, @Ignore, @Disabled, or a raised retries/retry count in a runner config. The failure was silenced rather than classified, and 15.3 QA-A-05 requires product, test or environment named first

forcing_classes.label: Coverage dropped on a changed path
forcing_classes.why: a coverage threshold number falls in the diff (fail_under in .coveragerc, setup.cfg or pyproject.toml, coverageThreshold in jest.config, a lowered minimum in a CI step), or a source file changed in this range with no test file changed alongside it and no coverage report showing that path already exercised

forcing_classes.label: Test deleted with its subject alive
forcing_classes.why: git diff --diff-filter=D lists a test file, or a test function disappears from a file, while the symbol it named still resolves in the tree (grep the removed test's target name outside the test paths and it is still defined). Removing the test of live code removes evidence, and it is a decision, not a cleanup

forcing_classes.label: Assertion that cannot fail
forcing_classes.why: the diff introduces an assertion with no failing input: assert True, assertTrue(True), expect(true).toBe(true), an assertion on a value the same line just computed, a try/except or try/catch that swallows the failure, or a test body left with no assertion at all after an edit. 6.1 E6 exists because a green that cannot go red proves nothing

forcing_classes.label: Fixture that does not exercise the real file
forcing_classes.why: the diff mocks, patches or stubs the module under test itself (unittest.mock.patch or jest.mock naming the same module the test claims to cover), or replaces a fixture file with one generated by the implementation. The oracle became implementation-derived, which is 15.4 level 6 and carries a circularity warning

forcing_classes.label: Risk accepted without coverage
forcing_classes.why: the persona forcing example in 25.2 verbatim: a row in the risk_coverage_map is closed with no evidence family attached, or untested_high_risk_paths is non-empty while release_recommendation says ready. A human accepts that risk; the pack never does

forcing_classes.label: CI quality gate change or bypass
forcing_classes.why: the diff adds continue-on-error: true, allow_failure: true, '|| true' after a test or lint command, an added skip-ci or no-verify path, or removes a required check from a workflow. 15.3 QA-A-22 requires the false-positive, false-negative and bypass analysis before this lands

work_classes.name: QA campaign / regression / exploratory testing
work_classes.role: primary: the class this lens is written for (persona doc 3.1)

work_classes.name: defect / incident correction
work_classes.role: primary: QA-A-21 makes the defect reproduce before the fix and fail again when the fix is removed

work_classes.name: API or contract change
work_classes.role: primary: QA-A-03 and QA-A-08, producer and consumer compatibility with negative and failure paths

work_classes.name: feature / capability
work_classes.role: supporting: risk-based selection of what the new behaviour must prove (QA-A-01)

work_classes.name: refactor / internal improvement
work_classes.role: supporting: behaviour must be unchanged, so a previous known-good release is the oracle (15.4 level 4)

work_classes.name: release / deployment
work_classes.role: supporting: QA-A-18 release smoke pack and QA-A-22 gate change; the release decision itself stays human (25.1)

work_classes.name: performance/cost optimization
work_classes.role: supporting: QA-A-10, a baseline and a threshold with the environment named

work_classes.name: security/privacy hardening
work_classes.role: supporting: QA-A-11 regression over auth, tenant and injection sensitive paths; the security lens owns the threat model

work_classes.name: dependency/platform migration
work_classes.role: supporting: QA-A-17 regression selection against the changed components and the historical defect map

risk_classes.reads: the axis this lens exists to move: how hard is it to prove the outcome, and does the oracle come from anywhere but the implementation. Drives the challenge question and the oracle fields
how many users and tenants a wrong answer reaches, which sets the test level (QA-A-01) and whether an E2E journey is worth its brittleness (QA-A-04)
API, schema and event consumers, and rolling deploys: raises E7 contract evidence and QA-A-08 to required
auth, secrets, tenancy and exposure: raises QA-A-11 and hands the threat model to the security lens rather than answering it here
whether a test run or its data setup can destroy, duplicate or silently alter records, including in a shared test environment
whether any evidence would run against live infrastructure or data. A suite pointed at production is a dangerous action here, not a stronger test
personal or regulated data in fixtures: QA-A-06 requires realistic constraints with no sensitive leakage, so a production dump is refused as test data
whether the failure this suite is meant to catch is detectable and recoverable in production at all (E15, E16); a gap here becomes an untested_high_risk_paths line
deleting a test, dropping a baseline or removing a gate is not cleanly reversible in practice, because nobody restores evidence nobody misses. Raises the forcing classes above
payment, billing and pricing paths raise the oracle bar to 15.4 level 1 (an approved business rule), since an implementation-derived expectation about money proves nothing

dangerous_actions: deleting, skipping or expected-failing an existing test (the pack raises the forcing class, a human decides)
lowering a coverage, mutation or performance threshold, or removing a required check from CI
adding a bypass to a quality gate (continue-on-error, allow_failure, '|| true', skip-ci, no-verify)
accepting a named risk with no coverage (25.2 QA forcing example: always human)
declaring a release ready, or merging on the strength of a green suite (25.1 reserves the release decision)
running any suite, migration or data setup against a production environment or production data
creating test data from a production dump, or committing any fixture carrying personal or regulated data
overwriting an approved visual or golden baseline (QA-A-09 requires the new baseline to be approved, not regenerated)
installing a test framework, browser driver or scanner into a repository that has not asked for one (22.1: detect, reuse, propose, install last)
presenting a PASS whose oracle is implementation-derived as if it were independent (6.2)

know_how.situation: a change has landed or is planned and nobody has decided what must be proven about it
know_how.brother_asks: which failures would be expensive, and which of them can only be caught at which test level
know_how.proof_closes: risks mapped to evidence families one by one, not a test count (6.3)

know_how.situation: a unit test is being added to cover new or changed logic
know_how.brother_asks: if the behaviour were broken, would this test go red for that reason
know_how.proof_closes: E6: the behaviour deliberately broken and the test observed failing, then restored

know_how.situation: an API regression suite is being built or extended
know_how.brother_asks: which negative and failure paths a consumer will actually hit, and which contract must hold
know_how.proof_closes: E7 contract evidence plus E12 negative and failure paths, not only the happy responses

know_how.situation: an end to end test is proposed for a critical user journey
know_how.brother_asks: what user value this journey carries, and which UI details can be left out so the test does not break on styling
know_how.proof_closes: the stable value path asserted, with the brittle selectors and incidental layout detail removed

know_how.situation: a test fails intermittently and the team is tempted to retry or skip it
know_how.brother_asks: is this the product, the test, or the environment
know_how.proof_closes: the failure reproduced and classified into one of the three before any waiver; the flaky waived forcing class fires until it is

know_how.situation: test data must be generated for a suite
know_how.brother_asks: which real constraints the data must satisfy, and whether any of it came from production
know_how.proof_closes: data generated against the declared constraints with no sensitive field present; a production origin is named or the data is refused

know_how.situation: an existing suite is being reviewed and its expected values are of unknown origin
know_how.brother_asks: where each expected value came from, on the 15.4 ladder
know_how.proof_closes: each check labelled with its oracle_source and oracle_independence; every circular one flagged rather than quietly kept

know_how.situation: a producer and a consumer are released independently and a schema is changing
know_how.brother_asks: which consumers exist, and which versions must interoperate during the rollout
know_how.proof_closes: E7 contract tests run from both sides, the old consumer proven against the new producer

know_how.situation: a visual regression check is being added or a baseline has changed
know_how.brother_asks: who approved this baseline, and what size of difference is material
know_how.proof_closes: an approved baseline plus a stated diff threshold; a regenerated baseline is not evidence

know_how.situation: a performance regression check is wanted
know_how.brother_asks: what the baseline is, on what environment, and what threshold counts as a regression
know_how.proof_closes: E13 with the baseline number, the threshold and the environment note recorded beside it

know_how.situation: auth, tenancy or user input handling changed and regression evidence is needed
know_how.brother_asks: which authorization boundary or tenant isolation could break without any functional test noticing
know_how.proof_closes: E14 over the sensitive paths: a cross-tenant read attempted and refused, an injection payload rejected

know_how.situation: accessibility regression checks are being added
know_how.brother_asks: which of the real accessibility requirements an automated checker cannot see
know_how.proof_closes: the automated pass recorded together with an explicit list of the manual gaps it does not cover

know_how.situation: a cross-browser or cross-device matrix has to be chosen
know_how.brother_asks: which combinations carry real user weight and real rendering risk
know_how.proof_closes: a risk-weighted matrix with the excluded combinations named, not an exhaustive grid

know_how.situation: a feature has many configuration flags and the combinations cannot all be run
know_how.brother_asks: which combinations are known-critical, and which interactions matter
know_how.proof_closes: pairwise or risk-rule selection recorded with the critical combinations covered explicitly

know_how.situation: the subject is a state machine, a workflow or an order lifecycle
know_how.brother_asks: which transitions are invalid, and what the system does when one is attempted
know_how.proof_closes: the invalid and edge transitions exercised, not only the intended path through the states

know_how.situation: the change depends on a network service, a queue or another process
know_how.brother_asks: what happens when that dependency is unavailable, slow, or returns a partial result
know_how.proof_closes: E12: dependency down, timeout, retry and poison message each exercised and the observed behaviour recorded

know_how.situation: the full suite is too slow to run on every change and a subset must be chosen
know_how.brother_asks: which components this change actually touches, and where defects have historically escaped
know_how.proof_closes: the selected subset justified by the changed components and the defect history, with what was skipped named

know_how.situation: a release needs a short confidence check that can run against the deployed build
know_how.brother_asks: which few checks would actually change the release decision if they failed
know_how.proof_closes: a minimal high-signal pack, each check tied to a decision, with the checks it deliberately omits listed

know_how.situation: a run produced many failures and someone must decide what they mean
know_how.brother_asks: which failures share one root cause, and which classification a human can verify
know_how.proof_closes: failures clustered by cause with the evidence for each cluster, never a per-test list handed over raw

know_how.situation: the suite is slow, noisy or nobody trusts it any more
know_how.brother_asks: what each test costs in runtime and flakiness, and what it has ever detected
know_how.proof_closes: runtime, flake rate, redundancy and defect-detection value per area, with the removals proposed as decisions

know_how.situation: a defect was found and a fix is being written
know_how.brother_asks: can the exact reported failure be reproduced by a test before the fix
know_how.proof_closes: the regression test failing on the unfixed tree, passing on the fixed tree, and failing again when the fix is reverted

know_how.situation: a CI quality gate is being added, moved or relaxed
know_how.brother_asks: what this gate will falsely block, what it will falsely allow, and who can bypass it
know_how.proof_closes: the false-positive and false-negative analysis plus the bypass path named; the gate bypass forcing class holds until a human accepts it

know_how.situation: any expected value is being written down
know_how.brother_asks: which rung of the oracle ladder this expectation sits on
know_how.proof_closes: the ladder applied in order (approved business rule, curated golden reviewed by a practitioner, independent reference implementation or query, previous known-good release, metamorphic or property invariant, implementation-derived, LLM guess) with levels 6 and 7 carrying a visible circularity warning

know_how.situation: the suite has grown top-heavy or bottom-heavy and the shape is being argued about
know_how.brother_asks: where the risk actually sits, rather than which shape the pyramid should be
know_how.proof_closes: the distribution of tests justified against the distribution of risk, with the mismatch named

know_how.situation: an expected result is needed and the implementation is the only thing that knows it
know_how.brother_asks: is there an approved rule, a ledger, a contract or a second tool that could say the same thing
know_how.proof_closes: an independent source cited per check, or the check labelled circular_risk and reported as such

know_how.situation: a suite is green and someone wants to know whether that means anything
know_how.brother_asks: which mutant would this suite fail to catch
know_how.proof_closes: mutants introduced and the surviving ones listed by behaviour, not a single coverage percentage

know_how.situation: the space of inputs is too large for examples
know_how.brother_asks: which property must hold for every allowed input, and which relationship must hold under a transformation
know_how.proof_closes: E3 invariants and E4 relations stated and exercised over generated input, with the generator's bounds recorded

know_how.situation: two services are released on different schedules
know_how.brother_asks: which side owns the contract, and which versions must interoperate
know_how.proof_closes: producer and consumer contract evidence, both directions, pinned to the versions actually deployed together

know_how.situation: the logic is a table of conditions or a lifecycle of states
know_how.brother_asks: which rows of the decision table and which transitions are unreachable, invalid, or untested
know_how.proof_closes: the table or transition set enumerated and each row or edge marked covered or NO-DATA

know_how.situation: the parameter space is combinatorial
know_how.brother_asks: which interactions between parameters have ever caused a defect
know_how.proof_closes: a pairwise or n-wise selection recorded with the rule that produced it and the combinations deliberately left out

know_how.situation: a test result is not reproducible run to run
know_how.brother_asks: which of time, ordering, shared state, concurrency, network or data leaked into the test
know_how.proof_closes: the non-determinism source identified and removed or pinned, then the same suite repeated N times with one outcome

know_how.situation: tests share a database, a tenant or a fixture file
know_how.brother_asks: what state each test assumes on entry and leaves on exit
know_how.proof_closes: setup and teardown made explicit, the suite proven to pass in a shuffled order as well as its usual one

know_how.situation: an end to end suite breaks on changes that did not break the product
know_how.brother_asks: which assertions are about user value and which are about incidental structure
know_how.proof_closes: the brittle assertions replaced or dropped, the value assertions kept, and the run time and failure rate measured before and after

know_how.situation: latency, throughput or resilience is part of the requirement
know_how.brother_asks: what the number must be, measured where, under what load, and what happens when a dependency degrades
know_how.proof_closes: E13 with a baseline, a threshold and the environment named, plus E12 for the degraded paths

know_how.situation: a defect reached users despite the existing gates
know_how.brother_asks: which gate should have caught it, and why it did not
know_how.proof_closes: the escape traced to a specific missing or passing gate, and the new evidence proven to fail on the unfixed tree

know_how.situation: the whole suite cannot run on every change
know_how.brother_asks: what the selection rule is, and what it knowingly does not run
know_how.proof_closes: the selection rule written down, the skipped areas listed as NO-DATA rather than assumed safe

know_how.situation: a gate exists but people route around it
know_how.brother_asks: who can bypass this gate, how often it has been bypassed, and what it costs when it fires wrongly
know_how.proof_closes: the bypass path documented and its use counted; a gate nobody can bypass and nobody trusts is reported as a finding

tool_adapters.absent: NO-DATA: no Playwright in this repository, browser journey evidence was not gathered here
NO-DATA: no Cypress in this repository

tool_adapters.detect: the repository's own documented command (README, Makefile, package.json scripts, project CLAUDE.md), never an invented invocation; pytest --version, npx jest --version, npx vitest --version, mvn -v as fallbacks
tool_adapters.absent: NO-DATA: no runner command is documented, so no functional evidence was produced
NO-DATA: no Newman or Postman collection runner, API regression was not run from a collection

tool_adapters.detect: pact-broker version, or a schema file present (openapi.yaml, *.proto, *.avsc)
tool_adapters.absent: NO-DATA: no contract tooling and no schema artifact, compatibility was not proven

tool_adapters.detect: a JUnit XML or allure-results directory produced by the run
tool_adapters.absent: NO-DATA: the run produced no machine-readable result file, so failures were not clustered

tool_adapters.detect: mutmut --version, npx stryker --version, or mvn org.pitest:pitest-maven:help
tool_adapters.mutates_note: mutates the working tree while it runs; run it on a clean tree and confirm the tree is restored afterwards
tool_adapters.absent: NO-DATA: no mutation tool native to this language is installed, so E6 was met by hand-inverting the named behaviour or it is NO-DATA
NO-DATA: no load tool present, performance claims are unmeasured
NO-DATA: no automated accessibility scanner, and the manual gaps remain unlisted

tool_adapters.detect: zap.sh -version, or the repository's own approved scanner command
tool_adapters.absent: NO-DATA: no approved security scanner is configured; this pack never installs one (22.1)

tool_adapters.detect: the repository's own configured test management API, if any
tool_adapters.mutates_note: writes runs to an external system; never called without explicit human authorization
tool_adapters.absent: NO-DATA: no test management system configured, and 15.6 makes this a soft dependency, never a hard one

provenance: 3.3 practitioner lens list and the qa-engineer challenge question
4.1 intake sequence (stage 0 orientation, stage 2 question value test, stage 3 profession-aware challenge)
15.3 QA automation use-case library (QA-A-01 to QA-A-22)
25.2 persona forcing examples (QA: risk accepted without coverage)
intake_dimensions: risk and user or business impact
test level best suited to the risk

fixture.must_infer_why: the manifest string is expected inside package.json, which door.MANIFEST_FILENAMES allows; the three path signals each match on their own, so the fixture stays green if one signal is later narrowed
fixture.must_not_infer_why: none of these may infer qa-engineer. The first two belong to data-science (which sorts ahead of this lens anyway), and the last three are the everyday shape of a repository that merely has tests: a plain tests/ directory must never win this lens, which is why no signal above names one

required_evidence_families_why.E1: Example-based functional tests: the persona's own working material: known input to expected output is what a suite is made of, and 6.1 calls it the weakest family when the expected output came from the same implementation, which is exactly the failure this lens exists to catch (15.4 levels 6 and 7)
required_evidence_families_why.E3: Property-based and invariant tests: 15.5 names property testing as a know-how module: where the expected value cannot be enumerated, an invariant (output cardinality bounded by the relationship, an idempotent operation changing state once) proves more per test than another example, and it is the family that survives a refactor of the implementation
required_evidence_families_why.E4: Metamorphic tests: 15.5 names metamorphic testing beside property testing, and 6.1 gives the QA-shaped instances: an irrelevant record must not move a metric, a commutative input set must not change the aggregate, a replayed event with the same idempotency key must not duplicate the effect. It is the answer to the challenge question when no independent oracle exists
required_evidence_families_why.E6: Mutation tests: 6.1 calls mutation testing central to the 'green can prove nothing' philosophy and 15.3 QA-A-02 makes it the critical evidence for any added unit test: breaking the behaviour deliberately and watching the test fail is the only proof that the test can fail for the right reason
required_evidence_families_why.E12: Fault injection and resilience tests: 15.3 QA-A-16 is a fault-injection suite and QA-A-03 requires negative and failure paths: dependency unavailable, timeout, partial failure, retry, poison message. A suite that only exercises the happy path leaves the expensive failures unmeasured
required_evidence_families_why.E2: Independent business oracle: the challenge question is about oracle independence, and 15.4 ranks an approved business rule or externally authoritative source first. Required whenever the answer to the challenge question is that the failure would be expensive
required_evidence_families_why.E9: Golden and replay tests: 15.3 QA-A-09 (approved visual baseline) and QA-A-21 (the exact defect reproduced before the fix) both rest on a captured, human-approved fixture rather than a value the implementation produced today

risk_coverage_map.meaning: each risk this change carries, and the specific evidence that covers it, in plain words. Not a test count: 6.3 says the target metric is risk coverage, and '137 tests passed' is not an answer.
risk_coverage_map.filled_by: file: the risk list written at intake (persona doc 4.1 stage 1 'provisional risk class') paired with the evidence family id that covers each row; NO-DATA when no risk list was written

oracle_source.meaning: where each expected result came from, on the 15.4 ladder: approved business rule, curated golden reviewed by a practitioner, independent reference implementation or query, previous known-good release, metamorphic or property invariant, implementation-derived, or an LLM guess with no source.
oracle_source.filled_by: file: the value stated per check, using the 6.2 vocabulary (requirement, business_rule, independent_query, reference_impl, prior_release, generated_from_impl, human_observation, none)

oracle_independence.meaning: whether the oracle can fail independently of the code under test: independent, partially independent, circular risk, or unknown. Levels 6 and 7 of the 15.4 ladder carry a visible circularity warning.
oracle_independence.filled_by: file: the 6.2 value per check (independent, partially_independent, circular_risk, unknown); a PASS whose oracle is generated_from_impl is reported with that word beside it, never as a plain PASS

tests_added_changed_removed.meaning: the three counts and the names, so a removal is visible rather than netted out against an addition.
tests_added_changed_removed.filled_by: command: git diff --numstat and git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only over the change range, restricted to the repository's own test paths

mutation_sensitivity.meaning: which claimed behaviours were deliberately broken and whether the evidence failed. The E6 result stated per behaviour, not as a suite-wide score.
mutation_sensitivity.filled_by: command: the repository's own mutation runner (mutmut run, npx stryker run, mvn org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage) or a hand-applied inversion re-run; NO-DATA when no mutant was introduced, never a pass

flaky_status.meaning: every test that failed non-deterministically in this range, and its classification: product defect, test defect, or environment (15.5 flakiness classification, 15.3 QA-A-05).
flaky_status.filled_by: command: the same suite re-run N times with the runner's own repeat flag (pytest --count, npx playwright test --repeat-each), the differing outcomes listed; NO-DATA when the suite was run once

environments_and_data.meaning: which environment the evidence ran in and where the test data came from, including whether any of it originated in production (15.3 QA-A-06 requires realistic constraints and no sensitive leakage).
environments_and_data.filled_by: file: the environment name and data source per run; a production-derived dataset is named as such or the field is NO-DATA

untested_high_risk_paths.meaning: the paths this change touches that carry real risk and were not exercised, said out loud. 6.3's honest shape: 'NO-DATA: behaviour under provider timeout has not been exercised.'
untested_high_risk_paths.filled_by: file: the risk_coverage_map rows with no evidence family attached, restated as NO-DATA lines; an empty list is only correct when the map has no uncovered row

defect_escape_impact.meaning: for a defect-driven change, what escaped to users, how it escaped the existing gates, and which gate now catches it (15.5 defect escape analysis, 15.3 QA-A-21).
defect_escape_impact.filled_by: file: the defect reference plus the regression test name; NO-DATA when the work is not defect-driven

release_recommendation.meaning: what the evidence supports, kept separate from the release decision itself. 25.1 reserves the release to the human, so this field is a recommendation and never a verdict.
release_recommendation.filled_by: file: one of ready-on-this-evidence, ready-with-named-gaps, or not-ready, followed by the named gaps; the human decision is recorded in its own field by core

gate_changes.meaning: any change to a CI quality gate in this range: a threshold moved, a step made non-blocking, a bypass added (15.3 QA-A-22).
gate_changes.filled_by: command: git diff over the CI configuration paths, reading for continue-on-error, allow_failure, '|| true' appended to a test command, and lowered threshold numbers; NO-DATA when no CI file changed
